title: Order on time, check every delivery, compare true cost

say: Order on time, check every delivery, and compare the true cost.
This is the video for module two of Supply Chain and Raw Materials Sourcing: planning, checking and costing your supply.
Most stockouts are not caused by the supplier alone. They happen because the order was placed too late.

say: The reorder point is the stock level that tells you: order now. You need three numbers. Usage per working day. Lead time, from placing the order to having checked, usable stock. And safety stock, the extra that covers bad weeks.
For example, Amaka fills an average of 100 bottles a day, and delivery takes 5 working days on average. So normal demand during lead time is 500 bottles.
On busy days she fills 140, and delivery took 8 days at worst. Worst case is 1,120 bottles.
Safety stock is the difference: 620 bottles. At about 60 naira each, that is 37,200 naira of cash tied up.
Her reorder point is 500 plus 620, which is 1,120. When her count falls to 1,120, she orders.
Use your last six to ten orders to find lead time. A supplier's promise of two days is not your lead time. Your records are.

panel.heading: Find your reorder point
panel.rule: Your records set the lead time, not the supplier's promise.

say: Compare the delivery note with your order. Then count and weigh on your own scale. A 25 kg bag that weighs 23.5 kg is short by 6%.

panel.heading: A six-step receiving check
items: Match the paperwork with your order
Count cartons, weigh a few bags
Check a spread-out sample against spec

say: Check that seals are intact and labels readable. Open several containers from different parts of the load, not just the top one, and compare with your reference sample.

say: Then decide: accept, hold or reject, and write it down.
Put doubtful stock in a marked HOLD area. Photograph any problem before you move anything, and send the photos to the supplier the same day.

panel.rule: Doubtful stock goes to a HOLD area, never into production.

say: Store well. Put new stock behind old, and use materials with expiry dates in date order. Keep sacks on pallets or shelves, away from walls, to reduce damp and pests.
Heat and humidity spoil oils, sugar and flour. Keep chemicals, cleaning products and fuel well apart from food or cosmetic materials. And label every container.

panel.heading: Store materials safely
items: First in, first out; or first expired, first out
Off the floor, away from walls
Chemicals and fuel well apart from food
Label material, supplier, date and batch

say: Total cost of ownership adds everything it costs to get a material into production: price, transport, waste, extra labour and late deliveries. Funke's prices are illustrative.

card.title: Total cost: two shea butter suppliers

say: Supplier A charges 2,500 naira per kg with free delivery, so 62,500 naira. Only 1% is lost in straining, so each usable kilogram costs about 2,525 naira.

card.title: Total cost: two shea butter suppliers

say: Supplier B charges 2,000 naira per kg, plus 7,500 transport, making 57,500. Extra straining time adds 2,000 naira, so 59,500.

card.title: Total cost: two shea butter suppliers

say: But 10% is grit, so only 22.5 kg is usable. That is about 2,644 naira per usable kilogram.
The supplier that looked 20% cheaper is about 119 naira more expensive per usable kilogram, before counting late deliveries.

card.title: Total cost: two shea butter suppliers

say: Before you talk, know your best alternative, usually your approved backup supplier and their price. If you can buy at 2,550 naira elsewhere, you can calmly decline a rise to 2,700.
Ask about price tiers, payment terms and a fixed delivery day. Ask open questions, and let the supplier propose first.
Ask for replacement of material that fails your spec, and priority during shortages in return for regular orders.
If they move on price, trade something they value. Then confirm what was agreed in a WhatsApp message the same day.
To remember. Order at your reorder point. Check every delivery before it touches production. Compare cost per usable unit, not sticker price. A tested backup gives you strength.
And if a supplier suddenly asks you to pay into a different account, call them on the number you already know before paying.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Reorder point: normal demand plus safety stock
Compare cost per usable unit, not sticker price
Your backup supplier is your strength
Pay only to the account name you confirmed
